scoreReasons: Every on-chain settlement is public, with a transaction hash returned to the client. An exact EIP-3009 payment looks like an ordinary token Transfer plus AuthorizationUsed, so nothing marks it as x402 unless the settlement carries a builder code.

The x402 contracts (Permit2 proxies, batch settlement) share one CREATE2 address on each EVM chain where they are deployed, which makes those paths easy to index. The proxies' own events carry no fields, so amounts come from the token's Transfer log.
Facilitator capabilities (GET /supported) and the Bazaar resource catalog are public HTTP endpoints, and x402scan publishes an explorer and API.

The richest per-request data (which client paid for which resource, signed payloads, vouchers, screening decisions) stays in headers and facilitator logs. Only the offers of listed resources are public in the Bazaar, and credit-backed cloudflare:402 commitments never reach a chain.
Public volume counters exist but are contested: x402.org has shown the same Last 30 days values since at least 2025-12-14, far above x402scan's 3.02M transactions in the 30 days to 2026-10-19.

public.where: The token contract on each chain
public.how: Transfer and AuthorizationUsed events; the transaction hash also arrives in PAYMENT-RESPONSE.

One CREATE2 address on each EVM chain where they are deployed (the contracts README lists the networks). Batch channels emit ChannelCreated, Deposited, Claimed, Settled, Refunded, WithdrawInitiated, WithdrawFinalized and ChannelClosed; the Permit2 proxies emit parameterless Settled or SettledWithPermit events, not the x402PermitTransfer event shown in the spec's reference code.
Lists kinds (x402Version, scheme, network), extensions and signer addresses per CAIP-2 family.

public.where: GET /discovery/resources and GET /discovery/search; CDP instance at api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/x402/discovery/resources
public.how: Public listings with accepts entries, lastUpdated, seller-supplied tags and service names, and 30-day call and unique-payer counts; no API key needed on the CDP instance. Tags are free-form, not a category taxonomy. Since 2026-10-13 the CDP Bazaar screens listing metadata for prompt-injection risk and removes resources that fail.

public.where: https://www.x402scan.com and its API routes (buyers, facilitators, merchants, origins, registry, resources, send, wallets)
public.how: Operated by Merit Systems. Its API routes are paid with x402 ($0.01 to $0.02 per data call) and registry writes need sign-in-with-x authentication. Discovery reads /openapi.json with x-payment-info, then /.well-known/x402, and trusts runtime 402 behavior over static metadata.
RFC 9421 public keys for signature agents in cloudflare:402 and the http-message-signatures extension.
builder-code appends an ERC-8021 Schema 2 suffix naming app, wallet or facilitator, and service.

public.where: x402.org, GitHub Security Advisories, the repository
public.how: A Last 30 days counter unchanged since at least 2025-12-14 (contested), GHSA advisories, Cantina audit reports, changelogs.

private.why: They travel only between client, server and facilitator, including which client paid for which resource. PAYMENT-REQUIRED offers go to any requester, and the Bazaar publishes the offers of listed resources.

private.what: Facilitator logs, KYT and OFAC decisions, pending settlement stores
private.why: Operational data of each facilitator; nothing obliges publication.
Cumulative vouchers live in server storage until the server claims them on chain.

private.what: cloudflare:402 credit commitments and billing identity
private.why: Credit-backed payments never reach a chain; Cloudflare maps signature identities to accounts.
Nothing on chain links a wallet to an agent or a person, which is the root of the volume dispute.

GET /discovery/resources on public Bazaar instances and x402scan registry routes
ERC-8021 builder-code suffix in settlement calldata
